rubrics.justification: No image was provided, and the response fabricated assumed blastocyst features (expanded blastocoel, ICM/TE grades, expansion 3-5) rather than limiting itself to stating morphology cannot be assessed.

It integrates most relevant factors well, including age, tubal factor, ovarian response, endometrium, prior biochemical pregnancy, sperm parameters, and lifestyle risks, though AMH is unavailable and some interactions are somewhat generalized.

The reasoning is generally structured and internally consistent, but it relies on an unsupported assumption of a good-quality blastocyst and gives a probability estimate derived from speculative morphology.

Lifestyle counseling, SET discussion, and luteal support are guideline-consistent, but recommending PGT-A, ERA/EMMA/ALICE, and acupuncture in this young tubal-factor patient after only one biochemical pregnancy is more weakly supported and not routine guideline-based care.

Provides clear practical recommendations for current transfer and future planning, including smoking cessation, alcohol abstinence, embryo selection, SET, and uterine evaluation, though some suggested add-ons are not strongly indicated.
